newsitem.title: USA: Japan, U.S. in complete accord on forex - Mitsuzuka.
newsitem.headline: Japan, U.S. in complete accord on forex - Mitsuzuka.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Friday that Japan and the United States are in complete agreement on cooperation in currency markets.
He told a news conference after a meeting of the Group of Seven industrial nations that the United States shares Japan's concern about recent movements of the yen.
"We have completely agreed to cooperate in currency markets as appropriate," Mitsuzuka said.

The G7 statement, issued after the Sunday meeting, confirmed a February statement made by the G7 in Berlin. The latest G7 statement stipulated that excessive and significant deviations of exchange rates from economic fundamentals are undesirable.
Asked if the G7 wanted concerted intervention by G7 members to counter excessive currency moves, Mitsuzuka said only that the G7 nations would continue close cooperatation.

Mitsuzuka said he told officials from other G7 nations that financial institutions can now cope with non-performing loans. Japanese banks are saddled with billions of dollars in bad loans, a legacy of the collaps of the property market after the asset bubble of the late 1980s.
